# Release signing setup for simi-next-support-android

This document covers the one-time secrets configuration required before
the `release.yml` workflow can produce a signed APK that passes the
`signature`-level permission check for
`com.simiconnect.next.permission.READ_DEVICE_PAIRING`.

---

## Why the same keystore?

`simi-next-android` declares `READ_DEVICE_PAIRING` as a `signature`-level
permission.  Android only grants a `signature`-level permission if the
requesting app is signed with the **same certificate** as the app that
declared it.  Therefore this fork must be signed with the same `.jks`
keystore (and the same key alias) that signs `simi-next-android`.

---

## Required GitHub Secrets

Set these four secrets on the fork repo
(`SIMI-CONNECT/simi-next-support-android → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions`):

| Secret name                   | Contents                                                |
|-------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|
| `SUPPORT_KEYSTORE_BASE64`     | Base64-encoded `.jks` keystore file (see below)        |
| `SUPPORT_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD`   | Keystore store-password                                 |
| `SUPPORT_KEY_ALIAS`           | Key alias inside the keystore                           |
| `SUPPORT_KEY_PASSWORD`        | Key password (often the same as the store-password for PKCS12) |

You also need these three build-config secrets (or pass them as
`workflow_dispatch` inputs):

| Secret name                      | Contents                                           |
|----------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| `SUPPORT_RS_PUB_KEY`             | RustDesk server ed25519 pubkey (base64)            |
| `SUPPORT_BACKEND_BASE_URL`       | Backend base URL (e.g. `https://api.simiconnect.com`) |
| `SUPPORT_BACKEND_SUPPORT_PUBKEY` | Backend curve25519 sealed-box pubkey (base64)      |

---

## Extracting the keystore from simi-next-android

The keystore lives at (on the signing Mac, not in git):

```
/Users/dimitriosvlahos/Simi APK/keystores/simi-ads-next.jks
```

> Note: despite the filename containing "ads-next", this is the SIMI-Connect
> release key used across the fleet.  Check the alias and DN to confirm.

### Step 1 — Base64-encode the keystore

```bash
base64 -i "/Users/dimitriosvlahos/Simi APK/keystores/simi-ads-next.jks" \
  | tr -d '\n' \
  > /tmp/keystore_b64.txt
```

### Step 2 — Set the secrets via gh CLI

```bash
gh secret set SUPPORT_KEYSTORE_BASE64 \
  --repo SIMI-CONNECT/simi-next-support-android \
  < /tmp/keystore_b64.txt

gh secret set SUPPORT_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD \
  --repo SIMI-CONNECT/simi-next-support-android

gh secret set SUPPORT_KEY_ALIAS \
  --repo SIMI-CONNECT/simi-next-support-android

gh secret set SUPPORT_KEY_PASSWORD \
  --repo SIMI-CONNECT/simi-next-support-android
```

Each `gh secret set` without `--body` or `< file` prompts for the value
interactively, which keeps the password out of shell history.

### Step 3 — Verify the cert fingerprint

After the first release build completes, confirm the APK fingerprint matches
`simi-next-android`'s:

```bash
# On the signed APK output from CI (download from the Release assets):
apksigner verify --print-certs simi-next-support-<tag>.apk \
  | grep "SHA-256"
```

Expected SHA-256 (from simi-ads-next signing notes):
```
02:98:A5:A7:9D:EC:41:BF:27:17:D8:49:8B:61:8B:65:74:CE:19:9E:44:2F:3A:4E:C5:DD:33:BC:08:A0:D2:3D
```

If the fingerprint differs, the wrong keystore was used and the
`READ_DEVICE_PAIRING` permission grant will silently fail at runtime.

---

## Icon source

The workflow generates launcher icon PNGs from a single high-resolution source:

```
branding/ic_launcher_source.png   (512×512 px, RGBA PNG)
```

This file must be committed to the fork repo **before** tagging the first
release.  Without it the "Generate launcher icons" step fails with an error.

Sizes generated by the workflow:

| Bucket          | Output size |
|-----------------|-------------|
| mipmap-mdpi     | 48×48       |
| mipmap-hdpi     | 72×72       |
| mipmap-xhdpi    | 96×96       |
| mipmap-xxhdpi   | 144×144     |
| mipmap-xxxhdpi  | 192×192     |

---

## Triggering a release

1. Ensure all seven secrets above are set.
2. Ensure `branding/ic_launcher_source.png` is committed.
3. Publish a GitHub Release on this repo (any tag starting with `v`).
   The `release.yml` workflow triggers on `release: types: [published]`.
4. Alternatively use `Actions → release → Run workflow` for a dry run
   (set "Dry run" to `true` to skip the Release asset upload).
